{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-vt-class-std","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"34fd390188b9dd6304c1c0ae073b048b12104e600dec5b2ea77dbfe2a5465977","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-vt-class-std:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"0441bafe0dc257fd56d6bd0cd9054ad2b95889f94f5d3e5e6f98fb890bf902c4","source_liveness_sha256":"13f90fd88bb623234ea3628f2ee40ced3511148c14c82097743066ee414dd040"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Licensing, permits and the driving tests","heading":"C — Licensing, permits and the driving tests","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Licensing, permits and the driving tests (part one)

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
A Vermont resident who plans to drive in Vermont must hold a Vermont driver's license, and a new resident arriving with a valid license from another jurisdiction must get a Vermont license within sixty days of moving in [A01].
Why it matters: The sixty day residency clock is a classic test question and differs from the commercial license transfer window.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
A person who holds a commercial driver's license from another state must transfer that commercial license to Vermont within thirty days of establishing residency [A01].
Why it matters: Commercial licenses move on a shorter thirty day clock than regular licenses.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Licensing makes driving a privilege rather than a right, so a license holder must drive within the limits of the law and treat every highway user, including bicyclists, motorcyclists and pedestrians, with courtesy and consideration [A01].
Why it matters: The privilege framing explains why a license can be taken away.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
Vermont issues six kinds of license: the learner's permit, the driver's license, the junior driver's license, the commercial driver's license, the enhanced driver's license and the driver's privilege card [A01].
Why it matters: Knowing the list helps place every later rule on the right document.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
A Vermont resident must be at least fifteen years old to take the learner's permit test, and a resident of another state who is enrolled in a Vermont driver education and training course can also get a Vermont learner's permit with a school letter confirming enrollment [A01].
Why it matters: Fifteen is the earliest age in the whole licensing path.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
A permit applicant who is fifteen, sixteen or seventeen needs a parent or legal guardian to sign the application before taking the test unless the applicant is an emancipated minor, and a foreign exchange student uses a Foreign Exchange Parental Authorization form that a host parent cannot sign [A01].
Why it matters: Host parents are explicitly excluded from signing.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
The learner's permit is issued after the applicant passes the online permit test and pays the required fees [A01].
Why it matters: The permit test is taken online, not at a counter.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
A learner's permit applicant under eighteen must have kept a clean driving record for the previous two years, and anyone with recalls, suspensions or revocations should contact the DMV because an additional waiting period may be required [A01].
Why it matters: A clean record requirement applies even before the first permit.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A02
With a valid learner's permit you may drive anywhere in Vermont at any time, provided the front seat holds a qualified supervisor: a licensed, unimpaired parent or guardian, an unimpaired licensed or certified driver education instructor, or a licensed, unimpaired person at least twenty-five years old [A02].
Why it matters: The supervising adult must be in the front seat, not just in the car.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02
Before driving in another state on a Vermont learner's permit, check with that state's motor vehicle agency or its law enforcement whether the permit is honored there [A02].
Why it matters: A Vermont permit is not automatically valid elsewhere.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
To get a junior driver's license you must have held a learner's permit for at least one year and kept a clean record with no permit recalls, suspensions or revocations during the six months before applying [A02].
Why it matters: Two different clocks: one year holding the permit, six months clean.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
A junior driver's license is issued to a sixteen or seventeen year old who passes the required examination, and a parent or legal guardian must sign the application to give permission for the test [A02].
Why it matters: Age band and parental signature are both testable.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
Before getting a license, every sixteen and seventeen year old must pass a state approved driver education and training course made up of thirty hours of classroom study, six hours of behind the wheel training and six hours of observation [A02].
Why it matters: The thirty, six and six hour split is frequently tested.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
On top of the driver education course, a junior license applicant must complete forty hours of driving practice with at least ten hours at night, and nighttime means the period from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise [A02].
Why it matters: The night definition uses sunset and sunrise, not clock hours.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
An applicant may take the road test on a learner's permit that has been expired for no more than three years and was renewed before the exam, but a permit expired for more than three years requires a written exam before the road test can be given [A02].
Why it matters: Three years is the cutoff for skipping a new written exam.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
Driver education taken outside Vermont counts only if a certified or licensed driver education instructor taught it with both classroom and behind the wheel training, and a completion certificate not issued by a state agency needs documentation on state letterhead listing the program's minimum requirements [A02].
Why it matters: Out-of-state courses need proof of both components.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A03
A parent or guardian must certify the forty hours of practice driving, at least ten of them at night, using the Driving Practice Log Sheet or the RoadReady app, and the law requires those forty hours to be in addition to the six behind the wheel hours of driver education [A03].
Why it matters: Practice hours never overlap with the course hours.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A03
A junior license applicant must put a Social Security number on the application, or supply a Social Security Administration letter showing ineligibility for one, and must book an exam appointment [A03].
Why it matters: The Social Security requirement has a documented exception.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A03
The vehicle brought to a junior license road test must be clean, in good mechanical condition, legal, carry a valid inspection sticker and have a properly working emergency or parking brake, and failing to show a valid insurance card and registration certificate prevents testing [A03].
Why it matters: Missing paperwork cancels the test on the spot.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A03
The insurance card shown at a road test must state the name of the insurance carrier, the effective and expiration dates of coverage, the name of the insured and a description of the vehicle including its vehicle identification number [A03].
Why it matters: Examiners check every field on the card.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A03
An out-of-state junior driver's license converts to a Vermont junior license by passing the required examinations, proving completion of a state approved driver education program and proving an additional forty hours of driving [A03].
Why it matters: Six months of out-of-state junior licensing lifts the graduated provisions.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A03
Some DMV licensed high school driver education instructors conduct driver's license road tests, but only at schools that have enrolled in the testing program and only through instructors certified as examiners by the Department of Motor Vehicles [A03].
Why it matters: School road tests are limited to participating schools.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A04
A student who passes a high school instructor's road test gets a Driver Education Examination Certificate, and the license is issued only after that certificate, a valid learner's permit, a parent-signed application, the fees and proof of Vermont residency are handed in at a motor vehicle customer service office [A04].
Why it matters: The school certificate alone does not issue a license.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A04
A junior driver's license is a provisional license: the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles may take it away when your actions show you are an unsafe driver, and it can also be taken away when your parent or guardian withdraws permission for you to drive [A04].
Why it matters: Parents can end a junior license without any violation.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A04
A junior license holder may not drive a vehicle in the course of employment, such as delivering pizza, until the junior license has been held for one year or the holder turns eighteen, whichever comes first, and may never carry passengers for hire [A04].
Why it matters: Work driving and paid passengers are both barred.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A04
During the first three months on a junior driver's license the holder must drive alone unless a qualified supervisor is in the front seat, the same parent, guardian, instructor or licensed person at least twenty-five years old who may supervise a permit holder, and with one present the only passenger limit is the number of safety belts [A04].
Why it matters: The first three months are the strictest window.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A04
During the second three months on a junior driver's license the holder may begin transporting family members, and after six months there is no limit on passengers, but at every stage the driver may never carry more passengers than there are safety belts [A04].
Why it matters: The belt limit survives every stage of the junior license.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A04
No driver may use any portable electronic device while operating a motor vehicle, which includes reading and manually composing or sending texts, instant messages and emails, and the devices covered include cellular phones, personal digital assistants, tablets and laptop computers [A04].
Why it matters: The ban covers reading, not just typing.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A05
A driver's license is issued to eligible people aged eighteen or older who pass the required examination, and it allows driving any noncommercial vehicle except a school bus or a motorcycle, each of which needs additional exams [A05].
Why it matters: Eighteen is the full license age; two vehicle types stay excluded.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A05
For the full license road test a permit holder brings a qualified supervisor whose license is valid that day, the same parent, guardian, instructor or licensed person at least twenty-five years old who may supervise a permit holder, plus proof of insurance and registration for a sound, inspected vehicle with a working parking brake [A05].
Why it matters: The accompanying driver must hold a currently valid license.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A05
A new Vermont resident holding a valid out-of-state license, or one expired for three years or less, takes an eye examination to get a Vermont license, while a license expired for more than three years or no license at all means taking the vision, written and road tests [A05].
Why it matters: Three years of expiry is the line between an eye test and the full test set.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A05
A license is refused to anyone whose driving privilege is suspended, revoked or refused in any state until that action ends and written reinstatement notice arrives, to anyone the Commissioner has evidence cannot or will not drive without endangering others, and to anyone who is not a Vermont resident [A05].
Why it matters: An out-of-state suspension blocks a Vermont license too.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A06
A school bus with a gross vehicle weight rating of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, or built for sixteen or more passengers including the driver, requires a commercial driver's license with passenger and school bus endorsements [A06].
Why it matters: Sixteen passengers is the dividing line for commercial licensing.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A06
A school bus endorsement is required to transport school children for hire, such as in a taxi, or in a multifunction school activity bus owned or leased by a school, and may also be required when carrying school children in privately or school owned cars and vans [A06].
Why it matters: The endorsement reaches beyond yellow buses.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A06
Any licensed person aged sixteen or older may get a motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle permit by passing a test, and students who complete the Basic Rider Course of the Vermont Rider Education Program are exempt from the state written and skill exams for the endorsement [A06].
Why it matters: Rider training replaces both motorcycle exams.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A06
All DMV visits are by appointment only, scheduled through the DMV website, and an applicant who cannot keep an appointment should cancel or reschedule as soon as possible so the time can go to someone else [A06].
Why it matters: Walk-in testing is not offered.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A07
A hearing impaired applicant will be provided an interpreter if one is requested when the appointment is scheduled, and the Vermont Relay Service for text telephone users is reached by calling seven one one [A07].
Why it matters: The accommodation must be requested at scheduling time.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A07
The driving tests check whether you can read road signs and lights, know the state's driving laws, see well enough to drive safely, have safe and courteous driving skills, have any disability affecting safe operation, will maintain your vehicle and will respect bicyclists, motorcyclists, pedestrians and other drivers [A07].
Why it matters: The purpose list frames every part of the exam.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A07
The vision screening checks whether your sight meets the required standard of twenty forty, and an applicant who does not meet it is referred, at their own expense, to a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist who evaluates whether any restrictions belong on the driving privilege [A07].
Why it matters: Only an eye doctor, not the examiner, sets vision restrictions.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A07
The knowledge test is taken online and has twenty questions, each with four answer choices of which only one is correct, and you must answer at least sixteen questions correctly to pass [A07].
Why it matters: This is the handbook's own statement of the test length and passing count.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A07
An applicant who fails the knowledge test must wait at least one day before taking it again [A07].
Why it matters: The knowledge retake wait is far shorter than the road test wait.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F42 | anchor: A07
The road test is given only after every other part of the test has been passed, and the handbook expects at least forty hours of real driving experience beforehand, guided by an experienced driver or instructor, with at least five of those hours in traffic [A07].
Why it matters: Five hours in traffic is a detail inside the forty hour expectation.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec01-F43 | anchor: A08
During the road test you will never be asked to do anything against the law and no tricks are played, you must follow the directions of the examiner riding with you, handle the vehicle with skill, drive at proper speeds for conditions and obey signs and rules, and no animals are allowed in the vehicle [A08].
Why it matters: Examiner directions and the no animals rule are easy points.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F44 | anchor: A08
Failing the road test means waiting at least one week before another try, and after a third failed road test the minimum wait rises to one month [A08].
Why it matters: One week after a failure, one month after three failures.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F45 | anchor: A08
You must furnish a registered, inspected and insured vehicle for the road test from any state, a rental vehicle is accepted only when the rental company provides a letter accepting full responsibility, and a vehicle on dealer registration is accepted only for an immediate family member of the dealership [A08].
Why it matters: Rental and dealer vehicles have special conditions.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F46 | anchor: A08
No road test is given in a vehicle displaying agriculture, antique or exhibit plates, because the law restricts how those plates may be used [A08].
Why it matters: Restricted plates disqualify the test vehicle outright.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F47 | anchor: A08
A road test vehicle needs working headlights, horn, wipers, rearview mirror, tail lights, tires, steering, windshield, exhaust, brakes, fenders and bumpers, plus directional signals on vehicles made after the start of nineteen fifty-five and safety belts and defrosters on models from nineteen sixty-four on [A08].
Why it matters: Safety belts are a hard requirement for the test vehicle.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F48 | anchor: A08
The emergency or parking brake of a road test vehicle must be able to hold it in neutral on any grade where it is operated, both headed uphill and downhill, and illegal tinting of the front windows is not allowed [A08].
Why it matters: The parking brake is checked in both directions.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-F49 | anchor: A03
A holder of an out-of-state junior driver's license who applies for a Vermont junior license stays subject to Vermont's graduated license provisions unless the other state's junior license was held for at least six months [A03].
Why it matters: Six months of out-of-state junior licensing lifts the graduated provisions.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-F50 | anchor: A06
Carrying school children in a school bus the manufacturer rates for fewer than sixteen passengers requires a Type Two school bus endorsement on the regular driver's license [A06].
Why it matters: Smaller buses stay on the regular license with an endorsement.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec01-F51 | anchor: A08
No road test is given in a vehicle that does not have safety belts [A08].
Why it matters: A short absolute rule that is easy to test.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0020]

Misconceptions:
- A learner's permit holder may drive with any licensed adult: false, the front seat supervisor must be a parent or guardian, a driver education instructor, or a licensed unimpaired person who is at least twenty-five years old.
- Practice hours logged for the junior license can include the behind the wheel hours of the driver education course: false, the forty practice hours are required in addition to the course hours.
- A junior license holder may carry friends once the first three months are over: false, the second three months allow only family members, and other passengers come only after six months.
- Failing the road test and failing the knowledge test carry the same wait: false, the knowledge test retake wait is one day while the road test wait is one week, rising to a month after three failures.
- Any licensed driver's license counts for a new resident: false, a license expired more than three years means taking the vision, written and road tests again.

Mnemonics:
- Sixty to settle, thirty for the truck: sixty days to get a regular license after moving, thirty days to transfer a commercial one.
- Thirty, six and six, then forty with ten dark: classroom, behind the wheel and observation hours, then practice hours with ten at night.
- Alone, family, anyone: the three passenger stages of the junior license, three months each until the limit lifts.
- Day, week, month: the waits after failing the knowledge test, the road test, and the road test three times.

Glossary:
- Learner's permit: the first stage document, earned at fifteen or older by passing the online permit test, that allows driving only with a qualified supervisor in the front seat
- Junior driver's license: the provisional license for sixteen and seventeen year olds who held a permit for a year, finished driver education and passed the road test
- Driver's license: the full license for people eighteen or older, valid for any noncommercial vehicle except a school bus or motorcycle
- Nighttime driving: driving between thirty minutes after sunset and thirty minutes before sunrise, for the purpose of the ten required night practice hours
- Type Two school bus endorsement: the regular license endorsement for carrying school children in buses rated under sixteen passengers
- Provisional license: a license that can be withdrawn by the Commissioner for unsafe driving or by a parent withdrawing permission
